newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan retail sales on gradual rising trend--MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan retail sales on gradual rising trend--MITI.

text.p: Japan's retail sales are on a gradual rising trend, an official at the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) told reporters on Wednesday.

He said although retail sales had fallen 2.3 percent in June from a year earlier, a larger deterioration than in May, when they had only fallen 1.8 percent from a year earlier, particularly bad weather and lingering effects of the sales tax rise had pushed the figure down.
The official also said retail sales were expected to continue the gradual rising trend in July, although the figure was not expected to be particularly strong or weak.

Positive factors such as bonus payments combined with better prospects this summer after a lacklustre summer last year, when the country was hit by the O-157 food poisoning outbreak, were likely to be partly offset by weak corporate gift-giving demand, he said.
He said the June figure had been weak as a typhoon kept shoppers at home, especially as bad weather had fallen on a Saturday, hindering sales of summer-related goods such as air-conditioners.
One less Saturday in June this year compared with last year and the fact that many employees received their bonuses in July this year instead of June were also contributing factors.
Wholesale sales continued to be firm as industrial output was healthy, especially production in the auto sector. Wholesale sales in June rose 5.1 percent from a year earlier, the ministry said.
